issues.failure_explanation: The displayed equivalence is false as written. The left side uses the gradient at param^* and the direction from param^* to param, while the right side uses the gradient and normal cone at param. Also, the left supremum can be negative at a boundary stationary point, whereas the right distance is always nonnegative. The correct identity requires the positive part and the same base point on both sides.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equation with the correct identity using the positive part and the same point, e.g. \sup_{\param\in \Param\setminus\{\param^*\}} \langle -\nabla f(\param^*), (\param-\param^*)/\|\param-\param^*\| \rangle_+ = \textup{dist}(0, \nabla f(\param^*)+\mathcal{N}_{\Param}(\param^*)).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed equivalence between stationary measures is incorrect; the surrounding discussion of stationarity measures is unreliable.
issues.title: False stationarity measure equivalence
issues.why_classification: The error is a local false identity that is not used in the main proof; the main stationarity definition is given separately.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $h_{n}^{(i)}\ge 0$, $h_{n}^{(i)}(\theta_{n-1}^{(i)})=0$. Hence if we assume $h_{n}^{(i)}$ is differentiable, then necessarily $\nabla h_{n}^{(i)}(\theta_{n-1}^{(i)})=0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof assumes that because the majorization gap h is nonnegative and vanishes at θ_{n-1}, its gradient vanishes there. This is only true if θ_{n-1} is an unconstrained minimizer, e.g. interior. On a constrained set, h can have a boundary minimum with nonzero gradient. Consequently ∇g need not equal ∇f at θ_{n-1}. Counterexample: m=1, Θ=[0,∞), f(θ)=(θ-1)^2, h(θ)=2θ+ρ/2 θ^2, g=f+h. Then g≥f, g(0)=f(0), but ∇g(0)=0 ≠ ∇f(0)=-2. Starting at θ_0=0, the subproblem minimizer stays at 0, which is not stationary for f. Thus the key lemma and main theorem fail under the stated assumptions.

failure_location.quote: Recall that $\nabla g_{n+1}^{(i)}(\theta_{n}^{(i)})=\nabla f_{n+1}^{(i)}(\theta_{n}^{(i)})$ since $g_{n}^{(i)}\ge f_{n}^{(i)}$ and $ g_{n+1}^{(i)}(\theta_{n}^{(i)})= f_{n+1}^{(i)}(\theta_{n}^{(i)})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis that the surrogates are tangent at the previous iterate, i.e. ∇g_n^{(i)}(θ_{n-1}^{(i)})=∇f_n^{(i)}(θ_{n-1}^{(i)}) (equivalently ∇h_n^{(i)}(θ_{n-1}^{(i)})=0) for all n,i, or otherwise ensure θ_{n-1}^{(i)} is an interior minimizer of the gap. Without such an added condition, no complete source-supported repair is identified.
issues.overall_effect: Invalidates the iteration complexity and asymptotic stationarity results for general constrained BMM; the main theorem and its applications cannot be relied upon as stated.
issues.title: False zero-gradient inference for majorization gap at boundary
issues.why_classification: The defect invalidates the key lemma, the main theorem, and the asymptotic stationarity proof for general convex constraints. A counterexample shows the advertised convergence and complexity guarantees can fail, so the repair requires a new assumption or substantially new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: A3(b) only gives a quadratic lower bound on the majorization gap h_n. It does not imply that the surrogate g_n is strongly convex; strong convexity of g_n is only assumed later in A5(b). The proof therefore uses an unestablished hypothesis. The proposition can fail under A1-A4 alone when g_n is not strongly convex and has nonunique minimizers.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add A5(b) (or an explicit λ-strong convexity assumption on g_n) to the hypotheses of Proposition prop:parameter_gap_decay.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition is not valid under its stated hypotheses; its proof requires A5(b) or an explicit strong convexity assumption.
issues.title: Strong convexity assumed but not in A3(b)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local hypothesis addition already assumed in the main theorem where this case is used, so no substantive result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume \ref{assumption:A1}-\ref{assumption:A4} hold. Suppose that  $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} r_{n}^{2}<\infty$ and {$r_{n+1}/r_{n}=O(1)$}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof invokes Proposition prop:stationary_conditions, which requires r_{n+1}/r_n=O(1). Proposition prop:non-stationary_nbh does not assume this condition (it is only in A5(a)). Thus the proof uses a result outside its hypotheses. In the main theorem under A3(a), A5 is assumed, so the repair is to add A5(a) to this proposition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis r_{n+1}/r_n=O(1) (or A5(a)) to Proposition prop:non-stationary_nbh.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition is not valid under its stated hypotheses; its proof requires the radius-ratio condition.
issues.title: Missing radius-ratio hypothesis in non-stationary neighborhood proposition
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local hypothesis addition already assumed in the main theorem where this proposition is used, so no substantive result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \min _{W \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{p \times r}, H \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{r\times N}} f(W, H):=\frac{1}{2}\|X-W H\|_F^2,
Furthermore, the sub-level sets $f^{-1}((-\infty, a])=\{ \param\in \Param\,:\, f(\param)\le a \}$ for $a\in \R$ are compact.

issues.failure_explanation: For the NMF objective f(W,H)=1/2||X-WH||_F^2 on the nonnegative orthant, sublevel sets are unbounded: take W=0 and H arbitrary; then f(W,H)=1/2||X||_F^2, so for any a ≥ 1/2||X||_F^2 the sublevel set contains all (0,H). Thus A2's compactness requirement fails, and Theorem thm:complexity does not apply to MUR as claimed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a compactness or coercivity assumption/regularization to the NMF problem, or prove separately that the MUR iterates lie in a compact set and that the relevant sublevel sets are bounded.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed convergence and complexity guarantees for MUR in Corollary cor:NMF are not supported by the main theorem.
issues.title: NMF objective fails compact sublevel-set assumption
issues.why_classification: The application to NMF is a major advertised result; the missing compactness invalidates the use of the main theorem and requires a new boundedness argument or a changed problem formulation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, the sub-level sets $f^{-1}((-\infty, a])=\{ \param\in \Param\,:\, f(\param)\le a \}$ for $a\in \R$ are compact.

issues.failure_explanation: With λ_i=0, the CTF objective is ||X - sum outer products||_F^2. Taking one loading matrix to be zero makes the outer-product sum zero, so f = ||X||_F^2 regardless of the other loading matrices. Hence sublevel sets are unbounded, violating A2. Therefore Theorem thm:complexity cannot be applied as claimed in Corollary cor:NTF.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add compactness/coercivity or prove boundedness of iterates separately; otherwise restrict to compact constraint sets or add regularizers that make sublevel sets compact.
